transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` mutable receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` parameter, naming the return, and preserving the unsafe public target signature.

Attached the generated `slice_align_to_domain(old(slice)@)` precondition and `slice_align_to_mut_result(old(slice)@, ret.0@, ret.1@, ret.2@, final(ret.0)@, final(ret.1)@, final(ret.2)@, final(slice)@)` postcondition to the executable target; no assume_specification or target-body external_body is used.

Preserved the Rust 1.96 branch structure: `U::IS_ZST || T::IS_ZST` early return, `self.as_ptr()`, `ptr::align_offset`, `offset > self.len()` fallback, and the aligned split/raw-parts branch. The mutable split, private offsets helper, rest length/as_mut_ptr capture, from_raw_parts_mut construction, provenance/aliasing facts, and final-frame bridge are isolated in one named source-backed boundary because Rust borrow checking prevents exposing `final(slice)` while returned sub-slices borrow it.

Isolated only source-backed boundaries for layout/ZST queries, slice start pointer extraction, `ptr::align_offset`, private `align_to_offsets`, `split_at_mut`, mutable raw-parts/provenance/aliasing construction, and the proof bridge from Rust final-frame facts to the generated `slice_align_to_mut_result` vocabulary.
